findings.Quote: Two people had put a hand on the case and read it as weight, and neither had bothered to look at what was inside.

findings.Quote: Ten times the density Detroit had ever managed. Ten times the machines, ten times the networks, ten times the minds sitting inside them that answered when they had no business answering
findings.Note: repetitive triadic anaphora reads as rhetorical filler rather than earned observation, inflating scale without specificity
findings.Fix: vary the construction or cut to one concrete comparison instead of three parallel 'ten times' clauses

findings.Quote: every morning, every time, from the day she came into them
findings.Note: triple-stacked repetition for emphasis is a worn intensifying device that doesn't add new information
findings.Fix: cut to a single instance: 'every morning since'

findings.Quote: she couldn't tell you which morning it had been
findings.Fix: shift to consistent third-person: "she couldn't have said which morning it had been"

findings.Quote: the mismatch had quietly gone and stopped being a mismatch
findings.Fix: tighten redundancy, e.g. "the mismatch had quietly stopped mattering"

findings.Quote: a set of skills that couldn't be skimmed out of her
findings.Fix: clarify the image — skimmed implies liquid/theft that doesn't quite land; consider "a set of skills no one could take off her"

findings.Quote: She was staying.
findings.Note: Flat declarative closer with no concrete image or stakes attached; reads as a placeholder emotional beat rather than an earned statement.
findings.Fix: Anchor it to something specific she's staying for or in, so it lands as a decision rather than a caption.

findings.Quote: as mass with a grade attached
findings.Note: Abstract phrasing undercuts the otherwise concrete, physical description of how he carries things; it tells the reader his worldview instead of showing it through action.
findings.Fix: Cut to a physical detail: how he gripped it, slung it, hefted it without checking the latch.

findings.Quote: explanation was a kind of value, and she wasn't about to hand him any for free
findings.Note: aphoristic filler that states a worldview rather than showing the transaction's texture
findings.Fix: She didn't tell him. Let him wonder.

findings.Quote: the corridor a language he was relearning one word at a time
findings.Note: metaphor doesn't survive literal scrutiny — a corridor isn't a language, and 'relearning one word at a time' is abstract filler rather than observed behavior
findings.Fix: cut, or replace with a concrete beat: he touched the doorframe like he wasn't sure it would hold

findings.Quote: the anti-surveillance weave at its quiet work
findings.Note: personifying the jacket's function is a soft touch of purple that adds little; reads as brand-copy phrasing
findings.Fix: cut or state plainly what the weave does for her here

findings.Quote: Whatever had done it wasn't costing him anything he was willing to show.
findings.Note: Vague, slightly purple abstraction stating stoicism rather than showing it concretely.
findings.Fix: Cut or replace with a concrete physical detail (e.g., he didn't favor the arm, didn't flinch).

findings.Quote: the kind of line a building AI could have logged
findings.Note: Cute simile that reaches for cyberpunk flavor but doesn't quite land literally — an AI logging observations isn't really analogous to a flat spoken remark.
findings.Fix: Sharpen the comparison or cut: 'the kind of thing a sensor could log, not a person.'

findings.Quote: like it belonged to someone else's report
findings.Note: Odd phrasing — arms don't belong to reports; the metaphor doesn't resolve cleanly.
findings.Fix: Simplify: 'like it belonged to someone else.'

findings.Quote: something in his face had come loose
findings.Note: Stock emotional-shorthand phrasing for a character's guard dropping.
findings.Fix: Replace with a specific, concrete facial/behavioral detail unique to Kyle.

findings.Quote: like the hallway had tilted half a degree and he hadn't caught which direction
findings.Note: Overwrought spatial metaphor for mild disorientation; doesn't survive literal scrutiny (a half-degree tilt is imperceptible, undercutting the image).
findings.Fix: Cut the precise fractional degree, or replace with plainer physical cue (he shifted his weight, unsure).

findings.Quote: She could be anyone she decided to be, starting now, starting here, in a hallway, with blood on somebody else's arm and none of it costing her anything at all.
findings.Note: Telling-not-showing the internal reinvention moment; the abstraction ('anyone she decided to be') and the tacked-on 'none of it costing her anything at all' undercut the concrete details preceding it with a summary aphorism.
findings.Fix: Cut the final clause or replace with a concrete sensory beat that shows the decision rather than states its stakes.
